newsitem.title: USA: CME live cattle seen lower, feeders steady to off.
newsitem.headline: CME live cattle seen lower, feeders steady to off.

text.p: CME live cattle futures were expected to open 0.100 to 0.150 cent per lb lower while feeder cattle were called steady to 0.100 cent lower, livestock analysts said.

Carryover pressure in live cattle futures was expected from weak fundamentals including cattle that were carried over from last week's showlists and expected lower packer bids. Packers also have June contract cattle available this week, analysts said.
One analyst also noted that interest in beef on Friday may only have been retailer fill-in business for Fathers Day promotions and beef prices may weaken later this week.

Higher CBOT corn price indications and possible pressure in live cattle should weigh on feeder cattle futures. The index was only up slightly and demand for replacement feeders will be down if showlists continue to move slowly, they said.
The latest CME feeder cattle index was up $0.02 to $77.37 per cwt.
